nodes.name: Capacity of a discrete channel
nodes.section: 1. The Discrete Noiseless Channel
nodes.statement: The capacity $C$ of a discrete channel is $C = \lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{\log N(T)}{T}$, where $N(T)$ is the number of allowed signals of duration $T$.
nodes.statement_clean: Capacity is the asymptotic exponential growth rate of the count of admissible signals as duration goes to infinity.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Capacity from finite-state constraints)
nodes.section: 1. The Discrete Noiseless Channel
nodes.statement: Let $b_{ij}^{(s)}$ be the duration of the $s$th symbol allowable in state $i$ leading to state $j$. Then $C = \log W$, where $W$ is the largest real root of $\det\bigl(\sum_s W^{-b_{ij}^{(s)}} - \delta_{ij}\bigr) = 0$.
assumptions: Constraints expressible as finite-state linear graph
$b_{ij}^{(s)}$ are symbol durations from state $i$ to $j$
conclusions: $C = \log W$ with $W$ the largest real root of the determinant equation

nodes.name: Discrete source as stochastic process
nodes.section: 2. The Discrete Source of Information
nodes.statement: A discrete source is a stochastic process producing a sequence of symbols from a finite alphabet, governed by transition probabilities (e.g., $p_i(j)$ for letter $j$ following $i$, or digram probabilities $p(i,j)$).

nodes.name: Ergodic source / mixed source
nodes.section: 5. Ergodic and Mixed Sources
nodes.statement: An ergodic source is a Markov source whose every sequence is statistically homogeneous: letter, digram, $\ldots$ frequencies in a long sample converge (with probability 1) to definite limits independent of the sample. A mixed source is a convex combination $L = \sum p_i L_i$ of ergodic components.

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (Uniqueness of entropy)
nodes.section: 6. Choice, Uncertainty and Entropy
nodes.statement: The only $H(p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ continuous in the $p_i$, monotonic increasing in $n$ for uniform distributions, and additive under decomposition of a choice into successive choices is $H = -K \sum_{i=1}^n p_i \log p_i$ for some positive constant $K$.

nodes.name: Entropy of a probability distribution
nodes.section: 6. Choice, Uncertainty and Entropy
nodes.statement: The entropy of $p_1,\ldots,p_n$ is $H = -\sum_i p_i \log p_i$. For a chance variable $x$, $H(x)$ denotes its entropy. For two variables, $H(x,y) = -\sum_{i,j} p(i,j) \log p(i,j)$ and the conditional entropy $H_x(y) = -\sum_{i,j} p(i,j) \log p_i(j)$.

nodes.name: Entropy of an information source
nodes.section: 7. The Entropy of an Information Source
nodes.statement: The entropy of a finite-state source is $H = \sum_i P_i H_i = -\sum_{i,j} P_i p_i(j) \log p_i(j)$, with $P_i$ the stationary state probability and $H_i$ the entropy of choices in state $i$. Per-second entropy is $H' = \sum_i f_i H_i$.

nodes.name: Properties of entropy $H$
nodes.section: 6. Choice, Uncertainty and Entropy
nodes.statement: $H \ge 0$; $H = 0$ iff one $p_i = 1$. $H \le \log n$ with equality iff all $p_i = 1/n$. $H(x,y) \le H(x) + H(y)$ with equality iff independent. Averaging operations on the $p_i$ never decrease $H$. $H(x,y) = H(x) + H_x(y)$, hence $H_x(y) \le H(y)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (Asymptotic Equipartition Property)
nodes.section: 7. The Entropy of an Information Source
nodes.statement: Given $\epsilon, \delta > 0$, there exists $N_0$ such that for $N \ge N_0$ the sequences of length $N$ split into a set of total probability less than $\delta$ and a remainder satisfying $\bigl|\frac{\log p^{-1}}{N} - H\bigr| < \epsilon$.
conclusions: $\frac{\log p^{-1}}{N} \to H$ on a set of probability $\to 1$

nodes.name: Theorem 4 (Counting typical sequences)
nodes.section: 7. The Entropy of an Information Source
nodes.statement: Let $n(q)$ be the number of most-probable sequences of length $N$ accumulating total probability $q$. Then $\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{\log n(q)}{N} = H$ whenever $q \notin \{0,1\}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 5 ($G_N \to H$)
nodes.section: 7. The Entropy of an Information Source
nodes.statement: Let $G_N = -\frac{1}{N}\sum_{B_i} p(B_i) \log p(B_i)$ be the per-symbol block entropy of length-$N$ blocks. Then $G_N$ is monotonic decreasing and $\lim_{N \to \infty} G_N = H$.

nodes.name: Theorem 6 (Conditional block entropy $F_N \to H$)
nodes.section: 7. The Entropy of an Information Source
nodes.statement: With $F_N = -\sum_{i,j} p(B_i, S_j) \log p_{B_i}(S_j)$, the conditional entropy of the next symbol given $N-1$ predecessors: $F_N$ is monotonic decreasing, $F_N = N G_N - (N-1) G_{N-1}$, $G_N = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^N F_n$, $F_N \le G_N$, and $\lim_{N \to \infty} F_N = H$.

nodes.name: Relative entropy and redundancy
nodes.section: 7. The Entropy of an Information Source
nodes.statement: The relative entropy is the ratio of a source's entropy to its maximum entropy on the same alphabet. One minus the relative entropy is the redundancy.

nodes.name: Discrete transducer
nodes.section: 8. Representation of the Encoding and Decoding Operations
nodes.statement: A discrete transducer has finitely many internal states $\alpha$ and is described by $y_n = f(x_n, \alpha_n)$, $\alpha_{n+1} = g(x_n, \alpha_n)$. It is non-singular if a second transducer recovers the original input from its output.

nodes.name: Theorem 7 (Transducer entropy)
nodes.section: 8. Representation of the Encoding and Decoding Operations
nodes.statement: The output of a finite-state transducer driven by a finite-state statistical source is itself a finite-state source whose entropy per unit time is at most that of the input. Equality holds if the transducer is non-singular.

nodes.name: Theorem 8 (Maximum-entropy assignment matches capacity)
nodes.section: 8. Representation of the Encoding and Decoding Operations
nodes.statement: Let a constraint system have capacity $C = \log W$. Assigning $p_{ij}^{(s)} = \frac{B_j}{B_i} W^{-\ell_{ij}^{(s)}}$ where $B_i = \sum_{s,j} B_j W^{-\ell_{ij}^{(s)}}$ maximizes $H$ and gives $H = C$.
conclusions: Maximizing transition probabilities exist; resulting $H = C$

nodes.name: Theorem 9 (Fundamental theorem for noiseless channel)
nodes.section: 9. The Fundamental Theorem for a Noiseless Channel
nodes.statement: If a source has entropy $H$ (bits/symbol) and a channel has capacity $C$ (bits/sec), then it is possible to encode the source so as to transmit at average rate $\frac{C}{H} - \epsilon$ symbols/sec, with $\epsilon$ arbitrarily small. No encoding can exceed average rate $C/H$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9
nodes.section: 9. The Fundamental Theorem for a Noiseless Channel
nodes.statement: Two-part proof: converse uses non-singularity of the transmitter; achievability is shown either by typical-set coding or by Shannon-Fano binary expansion.

nodes.name: Converse: $H' \le C$ forces $1/H \le 1/H' \le C^{-1}$
nodes.statement: Since the transmitter is non-singular, the channel input entropy per second equals $H$ and cannot exceed $C$, so the symbol rate $\le C/H$.

nodes.name: Typical-set encoding
nodes.statement: Split sequences of length $N$ into a high-probability set of $< 2^{(H+\eta)N}$ members and a low-probability set of total probability $< \delta$. Encode the high set into channel sequences; use a marker-delimited longer code for the low set.

nodes.name: Shannon-Fano cumulative-probability code
nodes.statement: Sort messages by decreasing probability $p_s$; expand cumulative $P_s = \sum_{i<s} p_i$ in binary to $m_s$ places where $\log_2(1/p_s) \le m_s < 1 + \log_2(1/p_s)$. The codes are prefix-distinct, and $G_N \le H' < G_N + 1/N$, so $H' \to H$ as $N \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Shannon-Fano coding
nodes.statement: Encode messages by binary expansion of cumulative probabilities to length $m_s = \lceil \log_2(1/p_s) \rceil$, achieving average length within $1/N$ of $H$ per symbol.
input: Source distribution $\{p_s\}$ over messages of length $N$
Sorted ordering of $p_s$ in decreasing order
output: Prefix code with $m_s$-bit codeword for message $s$

nodes.name: Source on $\{A,B,C,D\}$ with $p = (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8)$
nodes.section: 10. Discussion and Examples
nodes.statement: For this source $H = 7/4$ bits/symbol. The Shannon-Fano code $A\to 0$, $B\to 10$, $C\to 110$, $D \to 111$ achieves the limit exactly with average length $7/4$.

nodes.name: Run-length-style code for biased binary source
nodes.section: 10. Discussion and Examples
nodes.statement: For a binary source with $p \ll 1$ for $A$, encoding via a special start-marker $0000$ followed by a binary count of intervening $B$'s approaches ideal as $p \to 0$.

nodes.name: Noisy discrete channel
nodes.section: 11. Representation of a Noisy Discrete Channel
nodes.statement: A noisy discrete channel has finitely many states and transition probabilities $p_{\alpha,i}(\beta, j)$ giving the probability that, in state $\alpha$ with input $i$, the output is $j$ and the channel passes to state $\beta$.

nodes.name: Equivocation
nodes.section: 12. Equivocation and Channel Capacity
nodes.statement: The equivocation is the conditional entropy $H_y(x)$ of the input given the output. The rate of actual information transmission is $R = H(x) - H_y(x)$.

nodes.name: Capacity of a noisy channel
nodes.section: 12. Equivocation and Channel Capacity
nodes.statement: The capacity of a noisy channel is $C = \max_{P(x)} \bigl(H(x) - H_y(x)\bigr)$, the maximum being over all input distributions.

nodes.name: Theorem 10 (Equivocation = correction-channel capacity)
nodes.section: 12. Equivocation and Channel Capacity
nodes.statement: If the correction channel has capacity equal to $H_y(x)$ then it is possible to encode the correction data so as to correct all but an arbitrarily small fraction of errors. This is impossible if the correction-channel capacity is less than $H_y(x)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 11 (Noisy-channel coding theorem)
nodes.section: 13. The Fundamental Theorem for a Discrete Channel with Noise
nodes.statement: Let a discrete channel have capacity $C$ and a source entropy $H$. If $H \le C$ there exists a coding system transmitting the source over the channel with arbitrarily small frequency of errors. If $H > C$ one can encode so that the equivocation is less than $H - C + \epsilon$ for any $\epsilon > 0$, and no encoding gives equivocation $< H - C$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 11 (random coding)
nodes.section: 13. The Fundamental Theorem for a Discrete Channel with Noise
nodes.statement: Average frequency of errors over the ensemble of all random codes of duration $T$; show the average $\to 0$, hence at least one code attains it.

nodes.name: Typical input/output sets
nodes.statement: For long $T$ and capacity-achieving source $S_0$, transmitted sequences split into $\approx 2^{TH(x)}$ typical inputs, received sequences into $\approx 2^{TH(y)}$ typical outputs, and each output has $\approx 2^{TH_y(x)}$ reasonable causes.

nodes.name: Random coding: error probability $\to 0$
nodes.statement: With $2^{TR}$ messages randomly placed among $2^{TH(x)}$ typical inputs and $R < C$, the probability that a fan of size $2^{TH_y(x)}$ contains more than the actual cause is at most $1 - (1 - 2^{T(R-H(x))})^{2^{TH_y(x)}} \to 0$ since $R - H(x) < -H_y(x)$.

nodes.name: Equivocation converse
nodes.statement: If $H = C + a$ and equivocation $a - \epsilon$ were achievable, then $H(x) - H_y(x) = C + \epsilon$, contradicting the definition of $C$ as the maximum.

nodes.name: Theorem 12 (Reliable signal count)
nodes.section: 14. Discussion
nodes.statement: $\lim_{T \to \infty} \frac{\log N(T,q)}{T} = C$ provided $q \in (0,1)$, where $N(T,q)$ is the maximum number of duration-$T$ signals usable with error probability $\le q$.

nodes.name: Three-symbol noisy channel (Section 15)
nodes.section: 15. Example of a Discrete Channel and its Capacity
nodes.statement: Three-symbol channel where symbol 1 is noise-free and symbols 2, 3 swap with probability $q = 1-p$. With $\eta = -[p\log p + q\log q]$ and optimal probabilities $P = \beta/(\beta+2)$, $Q = 1/(\beta+2)$ where $\beta = e^\eta$, capacity is $C = \log(\beta+2)$.

nodes.name: Capacity for symmetric transition rows/columns
nodes.section: 16. The Channel Capacity in Certain Special Cases
nodes.statement: If each input symbol has the same set of outgoing transition probabilities $\{p_i\}$ and the same is true for output symbols, the capacity is $C = \log m + \sum_i p_i \log p_i$, where $m$ is the number of output symbols.

nodes.name: Capacity of a union of disjoint groups
nodes.section: 16. The Channel Capacity in Certain Special Cases
nodes.statement: If symbols partition into noise-disjoint groups with capacities $C_n$, the optimal total probability of group $n$ is $P_n = 2^{C_n}/\sum 2^{C_n}$ and $C = \log \sum 2^{C_n}$.

nodes.name: Hamming $(7,4)$ code
nodes.section: 17. An Example of Efficient Coding
nodes.statement: For a binary channel where each block of 7 has at most one error (8 equiprobable patterns), $C = 4/7$ bits/symbol. The Hamming construction with parity bits $X_1, X_2, X_4$ chosen so that three parity sums are even achieves $C$ with single-error correction.

nodes.name: Theorem 13 (Sampling theorem)
nodes.section: 19. Band Limited Ensembles of Functions
nodes.statement: If $f(t)$ contains no frequencies over $W$ then $f(t) = \sum_{n} X_n \frac{\sin\pi(2Wt - n)}{\pi(2Wt - n)}$ where $X_n = f(n/(2W))$.

nodes.name: Differential entropy
nodes.section: 20. Entropy of a Continuous Distribution
nodes.statement: For a density $p(x)$, $H(x) = -\int p(x) \log p(x)\, dx$. Joint and conditional entropies $H(x,y), H_x(y), H_y(x)$ are defined analogously by integrals.

nodes.name: Properties of differential entropy
nodes.section: 20. Entropy of a Continuous Distribution
nodes.statement: $H$ is maximized over a volume $v$ by the uniform with $H = \log v$. $H(x,y) \le H(x) + H(y)$. Averaging operations $p'(y) = \int a(x,y) p(x)\, dx$ with doubly-stochastic kernel cannot decrease $H$. $H(x,y) = H(x) + H_x(y)$ and $H_x(y) \le H(y)$. Under coordinate change $H(y) = H(x) - E[\log |J(x/y)|]$.

nodes.name: Maximum-entropy continuous distributions
nodes.section: 20. Entropy of a Continuous Distribution
nodes.statement: Among densities with fixed variance $\sigma^2$, the Gaussian maximizes $H$, with $H = \log\sqrt{2\pi e}\,\sigma$. Among densities on $[0,\infty)$ with mean $a$, the exponential $p(x) = (1/a) e^{-x/a}$ maximizes $H$, with $H = \log(ea)$.

nodes.name: Entropy power
nodes.section: 21. Entropy of an Ensemble of Functions
nodes.statement: The entropy power of an ensemble of entropy $H'$ per degree of freedom is $N_1 = \frac{1}{2\pi e}\exp(2H')$, the power of a white-noise ensemble of equal entropy.

nodes.name: Theorem 14 (Entropy loss in linear filters)
nodes.section: 22. Entropy Loss in Linear Filters
nodes.statement: If an ensemble of entropy $H_1$ per degree of freedom in band $W$ is passed through a filter $Y(f)$, the output ensemble has entropy $H_2 = H_1 + \frac{1}{W}\int_W \log|Y(f)|^2\, df$.

nodes.name: Theorem 15 (Entropy power of a sum)
nodes.section: 23. Entropy of a Sum of Two Ensembles
nodes.statement: If two ensembles have average powers $N_1, N_2$ and entropy powers $\bar N_1, \bar N_2$, the entropy power $\bar N_3$ of their sum satisfies $\bar N_1 + \bar N_2 \le \bar N_3 \le N_1 + N_2$.

nodes.name: Continuous channel rate and capacity
nodes.section: 24. The Capacity of a Continuous Channel
nodes.statement: $R = H(x) - H_y(x)$ and $C = \lim_{T \to \infty} \max_{P(x)} \frac{1}{T} \iint P(x,y) \log\frac{P(x,y)}{P(x)P(y)}\, dx\, dy$.

nodes.name: Theorem 16 (Additive-noise channel rate)
nodes.section: 24. The Capacity of a Continuous Channel
nodes.statement: If signal and noise are independent and the received signal is their sum, then $R = H(y) - H(n)$ and $C = \max_{P(x)} \bigl(H(y) - H(n)\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Theorem 17 (Shannon-Hartley capacity)
nodes.section: 25. Channel Capacity with an Average Power Limitation
nodes.statement: The capacity of a band-$W$ channel with white thermal noise of power $N$ and average transmitter power $\le P$ is $C = W \log\frac{P+N}{N}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 18 (Capacity bounds for arbitrary noise)
nodes.section: 25. Channel Capacity with an Average Power Limitation
nodes.statement: For arbitrary noise of average power $N$ and entropy power $N_1$, $W\log\frac{P+N_1}{N_1} \le C \le W\log\frac{P+N}{N_1}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 19 (Monotonicity of $\eta$ in $P$)
nodes.section: 25. Channel Capacity with an Average Power Limitation
nodes.statement: If we set $C = W \log\frac{P + N - \eta}{N_1}$, then $\eta$ is monotonic decreasing in $P$ and $\eta \to 0$ as $P \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Theorem 20 (Peak-power capacity bounds)
nodes.section: 26. The Channel Capacity with a Peak Power Limitation
nodes.statement: For band $W$, white-noise power $N$, and peak transmitter power $S$: $C \ge W \log\frac{2}{\pi^3 e}\frac{S}{N}$. For large $S/N$, $C \le W \log\frac{2}{\pi e}\frac{S+N}{N}(1+\epsilon)$. As $S/N \to 0$, $C \big/ W\log(1 + S/N) \to 1$.
assumptions: Peak power $\le S$ at all times
conclusions: Lower bound, large-SNR upper bound, small-SNR asymptote

nodes.name: Fidelity evaluation function
nodes.section: 27. Fidelity Evaluation Functions
nodes.statement: A fidelity evaluation has the form $v = \iint P(x,y) \rho(x,y)\, dx\, dy$, where $\rho(x,y)$ is a distance-like function measuring undesirability of receiving $y$ when $x$ is sent.

nodes.name: Rate $R_1$ for fidelity $v_1$
nodes.section: 28. The Rate for a Source Relative to a Fidelity Evaluation
nodes.statement: $R_1 = \min_{P_x(y)} \iint P(x,y) \log\frac{P(x,y)}{P(x)P(y)}\, dx\, dy$ subject to $v_1 = \iint P(x,y) \rho(x,y)\, dx\, dy$.

nodes.name: Theorem 21 (Source-coding with fidelity)
nodes.section: 28. The Rate for a Source Relative to a Fidelity Evaluation
nodes.statement: If a source has rate $R_1$ for evaluation $v_1$, it is possible to transmit it over any channel of capacity $C \ge R_1$ with fidelity arbitrarily close to $v_1$. This is impossible if $R_1 > C$.

nodes.name: Theorem 22 (Rate of a white-noise source under MSE)
nodes.section: 29. The Calculation of Rates
nodes.statement: The rate for a white-noise source of power $Q$ and band $W_1$ relative to mean-square error $N$ is $R = W_1 \log\frac{Q}{N}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 23 (Rate bounds under MSE)
nodes.section: 29. The Calculation of Rates
nodes.statement: For any source of bandwidth $W_1$, average power $Q$, entropy power $Q_1$, allowed MSE $N$: $W_1 \log\frac{Q_1}{N} \le R \le W_1 \log\frac{Q}{N}$.

nodes.name: Identities for joint and conditional entropies
nodes.section: 12. Equivocation and Channel Capacity
nodes.statement: $R = H(x) - H_y(x) = H(y) - H_x(y) = H(x) + H(y) - H(x,y)$.

nodes.name: Variational equation for rate-distortion
nodes.section: 29. The Calculation of Rates
nodes.statement: The rate-minimizing $P_y(x) = B(x) e^{-\lambda \rho(x,y)}$, where $\lambda$ is set by the fidelity constraint and $B(x)$ by $\int B(x) e^{-\lambda\rho(x,y)}\, dx = 1$.

nodes.name: Continuous-case quantizing noise
nodes.section: 28. The Rate for a Source Relative to a Fidelity Evaluation
nodes.statement: In the rate-distortion construction the residual noise in the recovered message is produced not by channel noise but by quantizing at the transmitter, analogous to PCM quantization noise.

nodes.name: Negativity of differential entropy
nodes.section: 20. Entropy of a Continuous Distribution
nodes.statement: Differential entropy is coordinate-dependent and may be negative; rates and capacities (differences of entropies) are coordinate-invariant and always non-negative.
